hardware.cpu: Apple M1 Max (8 performance + 2 efficiency cores; 32 GB unified memory; macOS 26.0.1)

gpus.name: Apple M1 Max GPU (32 cores, Metal 4)

toolchains.compiler: ParAC driver (patches 0001-0008, portable CPU solve), Apple clang 17.0.0
CMG MATLAB Coder C++ port (private), Apple clang 17.0.0

notes: Two devices. metal: the 27 cells of mac-20261031.json, unchanged (apxchol only, measured from PR #116 head 0009d670). cpu: this campaign, measured 2026-11-01 from 45f42824 (origin/main 468f3df5 plus the Accelerate adapter on branch bench-accelerate); every cell carries its source_commit.

Competitors are capped at max(20 x the best complete CPU apxchol total on the same matrix on this Mac, 30 s) per solve. A run over the cap or a process killed at its deadline is exceeded_cap; times are withheld and cap_s is kept. ParAC's runner has no per-solve cap: its cell (preparation plus three runs) is killed at 4 x cap + 300 s and its median-total run is checked against the cap.

8 OpenMP threads (the 8 performance cores). macOS has no CPU pinning, so runs are unpinned. Processes ran under nice 10, one at a time, on a shared host. Accelerate uses its own thread pool, which --threads does not control. AC/AC2 and CMG are serial (threads 1 for CMG).

C++ series: one warmup and three retained repetitions. AC/AC2: three processes after Julia's fixed warm-up fixtures. ParAC: three runs, no warmup (runner default). CMG: one warmup and three retained processes, solutions regraded with Julia outside timing.
RCHOL/pRCHOL use the portable Eigen PCG (no MKL on arm64) and the repository's macOS affinity shim, which disables their Linux-only thread pinning.
ParAC: portable CPU solve (patch 0008), ParAC's own zero-sum RHS (Euler's 'portable, own RHS' variant). The MKL and shared-RHS variants were not run (no MKL on arm64; shared RHS out of scope here).

Accelerate: SparseFactor Cholesky with Accelerate's default ordering (AMD) on the Dirichlet-pinned operator, SparseSolve plus refinement on the original operator; each solve counts as one iteration. A factor plus workspace above half of physical memory (16 GB) stops as oom before the numeric factorization. Accelerate's iterative CG was not added: its only built-in preconditioner is diagonal (Jacobi).
Packed CMG: the private MATLAB Coder C++ port built natively on this Mac (Apple clang 17), on the shared A and b. Canonical MATLAB CMG was not run: no MATLAB on this Mac.

apxchol CPU ran on all 27 matrices. Competitors ran on the 20 matrices whose every Euler series peaks at or below 13 GB, plus grid_3000. Other competitor cells are n/a with the reason: either the series' Euler peak RSS exceeds a 16 GB per-process budget, or the matrix was outside the competitor tier.
No competitor has a Metal backend; Metal cells are apxchol only.
max_rss_mb is the process peak from BSD time -l.
cap_rule: CPU: max(20 x the fastest complete apxchol CPU setup + solve on the same matrix on this Mac, 30 s) per solve; Metal: none (apxchol only)

columns.rel_res: largest ||b-Ax||/||b|| over the retained repeats, on the original system
columns.setup_s: seconds, from the repeat with the median setup + solve
columns.cap_s: the competitor's time cap, when one applied
columns.class: grids, meshes (meshes and circuits), ipm (linear programs), social (social and web graphs)
